newsitem.title: UK: Cocoa ends mostly firmer, Gauze remarks help.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa ends mostly firmer, Gauze remarks help.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa ended mostly firmer, helped by signs that the Ivory Coast was looking for higher prices.
Ivory Coast Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said in London he will go to Brazil at the end of June for talks on how to improve prices.
Cocoa, which spent most of the day trading around lows as active July went to 16 stg lower, recovered after Gauze's remarks.
By the close, July was last traded five stg higher at 1,029 stg per tonne, on volume of 1,319 lots of a total 3,823, recorded by 1615 GMT.
"It's a bit of Alain Gauze," was one trader's comment on the recovery . "The market is struggling with direction and remarks like that help," he said. "It's vulnerable to being moved."
"We are thinking about what to do to improve more cocoa prices," Gauze, who is in London for a meeting on coffee, told Reuters.
"The prices are good but we are looking to improve them," he added.
When asked if he would consider holding back cocoa sales Gauze said "This is something we are thinking about."
Gauze said he still expects a world cocoa deficit this year.
